question: An 8-year-old boy presents to your office for a routine well-child visit. Upon physical examination, he is found to have a harsh-sounding, holosystolic murmur that is best appreciated at the left sternal border. The murmur becomes louder when you ask him to make fists with his hands. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these findings?
analysis: The harsh-sounding, holosystolic murmur best appreciated at the left sternal border is characteristic of a ventricular septal defect (VSD). The murmur becoming louder with increased systemic vascular resistance (as when making fists) is consistent with the hemodynamic changes that occur in VSD, where increased blood flow through the defect leads to a louder murmur.
